output.title: Account locked — suspicious activity flag
output.content: If your account was locked due to a suspicious-activity flag (unusual location, new device, or an admin-triggered security hold), it cannot be unlocked by resetting your password. output.title: Account locked — too many failed login attempts
output.content: If your account is locked after several incorrect password attempts, wait 30 minutes and try again, or use the 'Forgot password' link on the login page to reset your password immediately via an emailed link. This is fully self-service — no need to contact support.

output.title: Two-factor authentication setup
output.content: Enable two-factor authentication from Account Settings > Security > Two-Factor Authentication. Scan the QR code with an authenticator app (e.g. Google Authenticator, Authy) and enter the 6-digit code to confirm setup. Save the backup codes shown at the end in a safe place.

**Subject: Re: Account locked, says suspicious activity**

Thanks for reaching out. I understand how frustrating this is—especially when you know the login was legitimate from your new laptop.

Based on your description, your account appears to have been locked by our security system due to a suspicious-activity flag. According to our policy, **accounts locked for suspicious activity cannot be unlocked by simply resetting your password**. This is a security measure to protect your account.

**Here's what we need to do:** Since the system flagged this activity as unusual (which can happen with logins from new devices or locations), **you'll need to contact our support team directly so we can verify your identity manually and restore your access**. We'll ask you to confirm some account details to confirm it's really you.

I'm here to help with that verification now if you'd like to proceed. To move forward, I'll need to confirm some information with you to verify your identity securely.

Is there anything else about your account I can help clarify in the meantime?
